Wald analysis of variance table for rrGDM models

Source: R/wald_test.R
anova.rrGDM.Rd

Joint Wald chi-square tests for each variable in a fitted rrGDM model, however many terms (design-matrix columns) the variable contributes. Where wald_test gives one test per column of the design matrix, anova() groups every coefficient that belongs to the same variable into a single test, so that:

  • a factor with several levels gets one test rather than one per level

  • terms such as x + I(x^2), poly(x, 2) or splines::ns(x, 3) are tested together as "the effect of x"

  • a variable that enters both the location model (formula) and the dispersion model (formula_sd) can be tested on both at once, or on each separately.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'rrGDM'
anova(object, ..., interactions = TRUE, separate = FALSE)

Arguments

object

A fitted model of class rrGDM, fitted with se = TRUE.

...

Not used. Only a single model can be supplied (comparison of several models is not supported).

interactions

Logical. Controls how terms involving more than one variable (e.g., x:f) are handled. If TRUE (default), a variable's test includes its main-effect terms and every interaction term it takes part in, i.e., it tests whether the variable has any effect on composition (or dispersion) at all. If FALSE, interaction terms are omitted. Variables that only appear in interactions are then omitted.

separate

Logical. A variable can appear in both the location model (formula) and the dispersion model (formula_sd). If FALSE (default), these are tested jointly in a single row (effect = "location + dispersion"), accounting for the covariance between location and dispersion coefficients. If TRUE, the location and dispersion effects of each variable get a row each.

Value

A data.frame of class anova_rrGDM, with one row per variable (or per variable and effect type if separate = TRUE) and columns:

  • variable: name of the variable.

  • effect: "location", "dispersion" or "location + dispersion".

  • terms: the model terms grouped in the test.

  • Df: degrees of freedom (number of free coefficients tested).

  • Wald: the Wald chi-squared statistic.

  • Pr_Chisq: p-value.

  • Sig: significance code.

Details

Intercepts and random effects are excluded.

For each row, the null hypothesis is that all of the coefficients involved are jointly zero. As in wald_test, structural zeros of the loadings matrix under constraint == 1 are excluded from both the statistic and the degrees of freedom. If the joint covariance matrix of the coefficients being tested is singular or ill-conditioned (judged on the correlation scale; reciprocal condition number below 1e-8), the Wald statistic and p-value for that row are set to NA with a warning, since the test is not meaningful when coefficients are unidentified or nearly collinear. If the Hessian at the optimum was not positive definite, the function stops with an error.

With interactions = TRUE the test compares the model against one where the variable is dropped entirely. With interactions = FALSE the test of a variable that interacts with others refers to its effect when the interacting variables are at their reference level (factors) or zero (continuous predictors).

As with wald_test, tests on location effects can be anti-conservative with few samples.

See also

wald_test for per-term tests, effect sizes and dispersion estimates.

Examples

set.seed(2)
# simulate data
n <- 25 # sites
p <- 25 # species

env <- data.frame(temp = rnorm(n), moist = rnorm(n))
eta <- as.matrix(env) %*% matrix(rnorm(2 * p), 2, p)
Y <- matrix(rpois(n * p, exp(1 + 0.8 * eta)), n, p,
            dimnames = list(paste0("site", 1:n), paste0("sp", 1:p)))

fit <- rrGDM(Y, env, k = 2,
             formula = ~ temp + moist,
             family = "binomial")
#> ℹ Preparing data
#> ✔ Preparing data ... done
#> 
#> ℹ Finding initial parameters (dbRDA)
#> ✔ Finding initial parameters (dbRDA) ... done
#> 
#> ℹ optimisation
#> ℹ Start 1/1: objective = 1670.1661
#> ℹ optimisation

#> ✔ optimisation ... done
#> 

anova(fit)
#> 
#> ── Wald tests by variable ──
#> 
#> • Interaction terms included in each variable's test
#> • Location and dispersion effects of the same variable tested jointly
#> 
#> variable  effect    Df     Wald  Pr_Chisq
#> temp      location   1  603.881    <1e-06  ***
#> moist     location   2  644.000    <1e-06  ***
#> 
#> ---
#> Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1
#> Tests on location effects can be anti-conservative with few samples.
anova(fit, separate = TRUE)
#> ── Wald tests by variable ──
#> 
#> • Interaction terms included in each variable's test
#> • Location and dispersion effects tested separately
#> 
#> variable  effect    Df     Wald  Pr_Chisq
#> temp      location   1  603.881    <1e-06  ***
#> moist     location   2  644.000    <1e-06  ***
#> 
#> ---
#> Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1
#> Tests on location effects can be anti-conservative with few samples.
